business_problem: Serco wanted to get more value from its ServiceNow estate, accelerate upgrades and internal automation, and build enough in-house capability to modernize employee and citizen workflows without relying on heavy customization or a tiny expert team.
solution_summary: Serco paired its existing ServiceNow deployment with ServiceNow Impact to turn platform governance, training, and delivery into a repeatable operating model. Impact introduced a Customer Success Manager, a capabilities map, and targeted accelerators that helped Serco assess instance health, speed upgrades, and plan a broader employee-services roadmap. IT Service Management, IT Operations Management, and App Engine remained the execution layer, but ServiceNow Impact provided the guidance and best-practice scaffolding needed to use them more effectively. Serco then used App Engine to launch a citizen-development community and release new applications, while Employee Center became the employee hub that consolidates request and approval workflows on one platform. Through on-demand training and Creator Workflow guidance, the company expanded internal certifications and micro-credentials so more staff could build, govern, and extend workflows without sacrificing out-of-the-box platform integrity.

data_flow: ServiceNow Impact governs Serco's roadmap, accelerators, and training, while App Engine and core IT workflows implement the resulting improvements. Employee requests and approvals now flow through Employee Center, and internal developers use the same platform patterns to build new applications and modernize business-unit processes.
business_outcome: Serco cut upgrade time roughly in half, completed 34 admin and developer training courses in a year, added 67 micro-certifications through citizen development, released 12 App Engine applications with more than 17 more in the pipeline, and created a stronger employee-service and modernization foundation for government-focused operations.
